## ISS-0031 (CRITICAL, PROD-01): Placeholder HTTP server — all API routes return HTTP 501

File: src/main.zig

The functions `runPlaceholderApiServer` and `servePlaceholderRequest` are placeholders that return HTTP 501 for all routes except /health/live and /health/ready. All real handler modules are already imported at the top of main.zig. The handlers exist and have proper signatures returning `HandlerResult { status_code: u16, body: []const u8 }`.

Fix: Replace `servePlaceholderRequest` with a real routing function. Requirements:

1. Initialize a DB pool from `config.db_url` using `db_pool.Pool.init(io, allocator, .{ .url = config.db_url, .pool_size = 10 })`.
2. Initialize all required stores:
   - `definition_store.Store` from `definition_store.Store.init(allocator, &pool)`
   - `engine_instance.InstanceStore` from `engine_instance.InstanceStore.init(allocator, &pool)`
   - `task_store.TaskStore` from `task_store.TaskStore.init(allocator, &pool)`
3. In the request dispatch function, parse `request.head.target` to route to the appropriate handler. The routing must:
   a. Match `/health/live` → HTTP 200 via `health_routes.handleLive(allocator)`
   b. Match `/health/ready` → HTTP 200 via `health_routes.handleReady(allocator, &pool)`
   c. Match `/metrics` → `metrics_routes.handleMetrics(allocator)`
   d. Match `GET /api/v1/definitions/active/:name` → `definition_routes.handleGetActiveByName(&def_store, allocator, name_segment)`
   e. Match `GET /api/v1/definitions/search?q=...` → `definition_routes.handleSearch(&def_store, allocator, query_params)`
   f. Match `GET /api/v1/definitions/:id` → `definition_routes.handleGetById(&def_store, allocator, id_segment)`
   g. Match `GET /api/v1/definitions` → `definition_routes.handleList(&def_store, allocator, query_params)`
   h. Match `POST /api/v1/definitions` → `definition_routes.handleCreate(&def_store, allocator, body)`
   i. Match `PATCH /api/v1/definitions/:id` → `definition_routes.handleUpdate(&def_store, allocator, id_segment, body)`
   j. Match `DELETE /api/v1/definitions/:id` → `definition_routes.handleDelete(&def_store, allocator, id_segment)`
   k. Match `POST /api/v1/definitions/:id/activate` → `definition_routes.handleActivate(&def_store, allocator, id_segment)`
   l. Match `POST /api/v1/definitions/:id/deprecate` → `definition_routes.handleDeprecate(&def_store, allocator, id_segment)`
   m. Match `POST /api/v1/definitions/:id/archive` → `definition_routes.handleArchive(&def_store, allocator, id_segment)`
   n. Match `GET /api/v1/definitions/:id/export` → `definition_routes.handleExport(&def_store, allocator, id_segment)`
   o. Match `POST /api/v1/definitions/import` → `definition_routes.handleImport(&def_store, allocator, body)`
   p. Match `GET /api/v1/instances/:id/history` BEFORE `GET /api/v1/instances/:id` → `instance_routes.handleHistory(&inst_store, allocator, id_segment)`
   q. Match `GET /api/v1/instances/:id` → `instance_routes.handleGetById(&inst_store, allocator, id_segment)`
   r. Match `GET /api/v1/instances` → `instance_routes.handleList(&inst_store, allocator, query_params)`
   s. Match `POST /api/v1/instances` → `instance_routes.handleStart(&inst_store, allocator, body)`
   t. Match `POST /api/v1/instances/:id/cancel` → `instance_routes.handleCancel(&inst_store, allocator, id_segment)`
   u. Match `GET /api/v1/tasks/:id` → `task_routes.handleGetById(&task_store_inst, allocator, id_segment, actor)`
   v. Match `GET /api/v1/tasks` → `task_routes.handleList(&task_store_inst, allocator, query_params, actor)`
   w. Match `POST /api/v1/tasks/:id/complete` → `task_routes.handleComplete(&task_store_inst, allocator, id_segment, actor, body)`
   x. Match `POST /api/v1/tasks/:id/assign` → `task_routes.handleAssign(&task_store_inst, allocator, id_segment, actor, body)`
   y. Match `POST /api/v1/tasks/:id/reassign` → `task_routes.handleReassign(&task_store_inst, allocator, id_segment, actor, body)`
   z. All other paths → HTTP 404 with JSON error body

4. For routes with path parameters (`:id`, `:name`), parse the relevant URL segment. Use simple string splitting on '/' to extract path segments.

5. For routes that read a request body, read the body from the request before dispatching. Use `request.reader()` to read the body into a buffer.

6. For query string parsing: extract everything after '?' in `request.head.target` and split on '&' and '=' to build a simple key-value table.

7. For the Actor context (tasks routes), derive a minimal default actor:
   - Use the `X-BPM-User-Id` request header if present, otherwise use a default UUID string
   - Set `is_operator_or_above = true` and `is_platform_admin = false` as defaults until auth middleware is fully wired

8. SECURITY: Do not interpolate any user-supplied URL parameters into SQL strings. All user data must flow through the handler functions (which already use parameterized queries).

9. Check the exact function signatures in each handler file before calling them. The handler files are:
   - src/api/routes/definitions.zig
   - src/api/routes/instances.zig
   - src/api/routes/tasks.zig
   - src/api/routes/health.zig
   - src/api/routes/metrics.zig

10. The HandlerResult struct is `{ status_code: u16, body: []const u8 }`. Respond with:
    ```
    try request.respond(result.body, .{
        .status = @enumFromInt(result.status_code),
        .keep_alive = false,
        .extra_headers = &json_content_header,
    });
    ```
    Then `allocator.free(result.body)`.

11. Use an arena allocator per request to simplify memory management:
    ```zig
    var arena = std.heap.ArenaAllocator.init(allocator);
    defer arena.deinit();
    const req_alloc = arena.allocator();
    ```

## ISS-0032 (CRITICAL, PROD-02): rowToDefinition never deserializes graph JSONB

Files: src/definition/store.zig

The function `rowToDefinition` at the bottom of src/definition/store.zig has this stub:
```zig
// Stub: graph column not parsed until pg.zig delivers real rows.
// TODO: parse JSONB text into DefinitionGraph when pg.zig is complete.
const graph = fallback.graph;
```

This causes `handleActivate` to always receive a Definition with an empty `graph` (nodes=[], edges=[]), which then fails graph validation in `store.activate()` → HTTP 422.

Fix:
1. Replace the stub `const graph = fallback.graph;` in `rowToDefinition` with a real parse:
   ```zig
   const graph_json_str = col.get(row, 5);
   const graph = if (graph_json_str.len > 0)
       parseGraphJson(allocator, graph_json_str) catch fallback.graph
   else
       fallback.graph;
   ```
   Note: `parseGraphJson` is defined later in the same file and allocates a deep copy that the caller owns. The `rowToDefinition` return value already owns the `name`, `version`, etc. strings. The caller of `rowToDefinition` owns the returned Definition and is responsible for freeing it.

2. Update the stale doc comment on `rowToDefinition` — remove the line:
   `/// NOTE: When pg.zig is fully implemented, real row data will be present.`
   `/// Currently all DB calls return QueryFailed so this path is never reached.`
   Replace with:
   `/// Parses a DB row into a Definition. Column index layout documented above.`

IMPORTANT: After this fix, the graph in every Definition returned from DB queries will be a deep-copy allocated from the caller's allocator. Verify that callers that call `freeDefinition()` also free the graph properly. Check `freeDefinition` in src/api/routes/definitions.zig to confirm it frees the graph nodes and edges. If `freeDefinition` does not free the graph, add graph freeing to it.

## ISS-0033 (MAJOR, PROD-03): Hardcoded exported_at timestamp in export/import

File: src/definition/export_import.zig

Line ~139:
```zig
// TODO: real timestamp — generate from std.time.timestamp() as ISO8601
const exported_at = allocator.dupe(u8, "2026-05-21T00:00:00Z") catch
    return ExportImportError.DatabaseError;
```

Fix: Replace the hardcoded string with a real UTC timestamp:
```zig
const now_secs = std.time.timestamp();
const epoch_secs: u64 = @intCast(now_secs);
const epoch = std.time.epoch.EpochSeconds{ .secs = epoch_secs };
const day = epoch.getEpochDay();
const year_day = day.calculateYearDay();
const month_day = year_day.calculateMonthDay();
const day_secs = epoch.getDaySeconds();
const exported_at = std.fmt.allocPrint(
    allocator,
    "{d:0>4}-{d:0>2}-{d:0>2}T{d:0>2}:{d:0>2}:{d:0>2}Z",
    .{
        year_day.year,
        month_day.month.numeric(),
        month_day.day_index + 1,
        day_secs.getHoursIntoDay(),
        day_secs.getMinutesIntoHour(),
        day_secs.getSecondsIntoMinute(),
    },
) catch return ExportImportError.DatabaseError;
```
Remove the TODO comment. The `errdefer allocator.free(exported_at)` line below is already correct.

## ISS-0034 (LOW, PROD-04): Stale 'pg stub' comment in pool.zig

File: src/db/pool.zig

Lines 1-5 contain:
```
//! Wraps the pg vendor module (vendor/pg/pg.zig).  The pg module is currently a
//! stub; all connections are held as placeholder state and actual SQL execution
//! returns QueryFailed until pg.zig is fully implemented.
```

Fix: Replace those three lines with accurate description:
```
//! Wraps the pg vendor module (vendor/pg/pg.zig).  Provides acquire/release
//! semantics over a fixed-size connection pool.  All SQL execution goes through
//! pg.zig which delivers real query results against a live PostgreSQL database.
```
